use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: C2 JU resolves dual designations by correlating two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.

scope_contract.goal_statement: C2 JU resolves dual designations by correlating two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation; C2 JU correlates them and thereby resolves the dual designation.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The dual designation is resolved, and each ballistic missile track reported on the interface represents a single data point.
in_scope_actions: Correlate the two eligible ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface
excluded_adjacent_actions: Using PPLI data to reduce surveillance track reporting redundancy (EC-G-000)
General protocol activities for minimizing future occurrences/duration of dual designations (EC-G-001)

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU recognizes that two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
The two ballistic missile tracks are eligible for correlation by passing the positional test: course differential, speed differential, and altitude differential.

The two tracks pass the required correlation tests and restrictions the required number of times before correlation is executed, including no conflicting Identity difference, no Strength field greater than 1 (unless set to No Statement), and no different Mode II codes while the local Mode II code is current.
Positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation are extrapolated to the same time.
The C2 JU recognizes that two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, and initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The C2 JU compares the locally derived ballistic missile track data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the ballistic missile track data received on the Surveillance NPG/interface.
When the two ballistic missile tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, the C2 JU deems them a tentative correlation.
Upon the next correlation stimulus, the C2 JU tests the same two ballistic missile tracks again.
When the two ballistic missile tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions a second time and no correlation restriction applies, the C2 JU processes the tracks for dual designation resolution.
The recognizing C2 JU transmits a J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to correlate the two tracks, identifying the Retained TN and the Dropped TN.
The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation.
The originating C2 JU holding R² for the Dropped TN ceases reporting the Dropped TN and transmits a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message after the J7.2 message.
Each ballistic missile track reported on the interface now represents a single data point, and the dual designation is resolved.

Diverges from Step 4: Instead of requiring the automatic pass of correlation tests and restrictions, the operator manually initiates correlation using the manual correlation capability, irrespective of the automatic correlation test criteria, correlation restrictions, or requirements; this manual path is not available for tracks of a different E/C, one simulated and one live track, or two remote tracks.

Diverges from Step 4: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the C2 JU alerts the operator to either (a) change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, allowing automatic correlation, or (b) transmit an ID Difference Report, allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.

Diverges from Step 4: If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other track has an ID of Friend, automatic correlation may be allowed despite the conflicting-ID restriction.

Diverges from Step 4: When processing the correlation and the Identity of the Retained TN and Dropped TN are the same, the C2 JU retains the associated identification data reported for the Retained TN.

Diverges from Step 4: When processing the correlation, if the ID or Identity Amplifying Descriptor of the Retained TN and Dropped TN are different and the difference would result in automatic acceptance of the Dropped TN ID/IAD, the C2 JU transfers the Dropped TN ID/IAD, Special Interest Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type to the Retained TN.

Diverges from Step 6: Instead of accepting the requested correlation, the responding C2 JU may respond with a reverse correlation, transmitting the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 6: If the correlation request is a manual correlation (RV=3) and the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held with an OCC, the C2 JU executes the correlation using the Dropped TN data and the Retained TN track number.
Diverges from Step 7: When a J7.2 message is initiated by own unit and a Drop Track message has not yet been received for the Dropped TN, the C2 JU retains the Dropped TN as a remote track.

Diverges from Step 1: When the dual designation arises from an initial report on ballistic missile contacts, track merging, simultaneous multiple launches, registration errors, time-of-observation differences, or high velocity contacts, the correlation may fail or produce erroneous results, triggering exception handling. Exit: the applicable exception-handling path is triggered instead of relying on the standard correlation outcome.

Diverges from Step 3: The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time; if more than 6 seconds have elapsed since the extrapolation time, the correlation test cannot be performed in compliance with this requirement. Exit: the branch terminates without performing the correlation test at that time.

Diverges from Step 6: Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless prespecified conditions exist; if a C2 JU receiving a J7.2 Correlation message holds OCCs on both tracks, or holds conflicting IDs on the two tracks while the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled, it shall reject the correlation and transmit a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection. Exit: the branch terminates with the J7.2 (RV=2) rejection message transmitted and the requested correlation not accepted.

Diverges from Step 7: If a ballistic missile track involved in the correlation is considered lost — the JU with R² has not received any local sensor data since the last transmitted update, or the JU determines the track is lost by other system criteria — and is reported with the Lost Track Indicator set to value 1, the reporting JU is assumed to have a TQ of 5 less than that being reported; for example, if a JU reports Lost Track data with a TQ of 15, a JU holding Tracking data may assume R² with a TQ of 11. Exit: the branch terminates with the assumed TQ/R² applied for the lost track in the correlation processing.

Diverges from Step 8: If it is determined that more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported, track decorrelation shall occur. Exit: the branch terminates with the track decorrelated.

missing_aspects: Specific exception-handling actions for each error-prone situation (initial report, track merging, simultaneous launches, registration errors, time-of-observation differences, high-velocity contacts) beyond triggering exception handling are not documented.
Recovery/continuation after a J7.2 (RV=2) correlation rejection is not documented.
Continuation of the drop-track reporting after the lost-track TQ/R² assumption is not documented.
Recovery/continuation when the correlation test exceeds the 6-second post-extrapolation window (e.g., re-extrapolation and retest) is not documented.
Continuation after decorrelation (e.g., subsequent re-correlation attempts) is not documented.

claims.content: The dual designation is resolved via correlation, and each ballistic missile track reported on the interface represents a single data point.

Upon acceptance of the requested correlation, receiving IUs retain the designated Retained TN and drop the designated Dropped TN. If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it drops the Dropped TN and transmits a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message after the J7.2 message. If the own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Dropped TN is designated as a common local track.

Upon correlation execution, the Retained TN is updated from the Dropped TN with Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, and Strength (if the Dropped TN was a local or common local track); any nonzero Mode I, II, or III IFF/SIF data from the Dropped TN is transferred to the Retained TN if the corresponding Retained TN data is zero.

The final identification state of the Retained TN is determined by the ID conflict restriction rules: if restricted and IDs differ, the last Identity reported for the Dropped TN is processed as an Identity Difference Report for the Retained TN; otherwise, specific ID/IAD and platform attributes are transferred.
After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3), the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.

The main flow, however, starts over by comparing track data, declaring a tentative correlation after one pass, and only processing for resolution after a second pass. This is a restart/contradiction: the use case starts after the outcome of the main-flow test sequence rather than at the initiating event. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Starting the track correlation sequence to resolve a possible dual designation is not supported by the cited cards.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception Flow claim 1 (diverging from Step 1) does not provide a concrete exit. It ends with 'triggering exception handling' / 'the applicable exception-handling path is triggered' without naming that path or defining a terminal state, so there is no clear outcome for the branch. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit recovery/exit behavior after track decorrelation is not supported by the cited cards; evidence is needed for whether the exception branch terminates, resumes, or continues.))
